This fix deliberately makes the order width-dependent again - past before the measure at >=1280, after it below - which is the round-1 swap restored, and the finding's own text concedes it by specifying a different order below 1280. Trading a closed finding for an open one is a worse trade at a 9.5 bar. Whitespace beside a sticky rail that fills on the owner's primary action is normal at the named benchmarks (Linear, Stripe), not a composition defect; asserting it is one, with the only proposed occupant being the object the lock places elsewhere, is taste stated as a defect.
sharpenedFix: Do not move .b-behind. If the panel still wants the rail's rest state answered, the only in-lock levers are: (a) give the rail an object that belongs to the present tense rather than the past - this same seat's 'undo-lands-below-the-fold' already proposes rendering the reversibility plate as the last child of .b-stick with a reserved 44px band, which fills the top of the gap, keeps one reversibility surface in one place, is identical at every width and touches no reading order; and (b) on the guest surfaces (states.desk, states.print), where there is no editor and never will be, treat it as proportion, not content - narrow the [data-medium='full'] .b-two first track from 360px so the horizon column is sized to its 327px placard rather than to an editor it does not host.
